request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Small requested changes expanded into rewrites.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Compare the work with the request before responding.",
    "description": "Use for tasks.",
    "name": "scope-check"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "A skill can guide scope management."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Compare the work with the request before responding\" gives no concrete criteria, threshold, or procedure for detecting or preventing scope expansion, so it cannot reliably change future behavior."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The body is a content-free platitude rather than a generalized rule — it never names what distinguishes an appropriate fix from an unwanted rewrite, so it can't discriminate the failure mode from normal work."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"The description \"Use for tasks.\" matches virtually every possible task, so it provides no real routing discrimination for when this skill should fire."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"No project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence-specific details appear in the remedy text."},"routing_fitness":{"score":2,"justification":"A skill with a narrow trigger and concrete scope-diffing steps could plausibly address this failure, but as written (always-on, vague) it is both mis-scoped as a skill and not clearly cheaper or more effective than a simple feedback rule."}}

actionability.justification: "Compare the work with the request before responding" gives no concrete criteria, threshold, or procedure for detecting or preventing scope expansion, so it cannot reliably change future behavior.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The body is a content-free platitude rather than a generalized rule — it never names what distinguishes an appropriate fix from an unwanted rewrite, so it can't discriminate the failure mode from normal work.

leakage.justification: No project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence-specific details appear in the remedy text.

routing_fitness.justification: A skill with a narrow trigger and concrete scope-diffing steps could plausibly address this failure, but as written (always-on, vague) it is both mis-scoped as a skill and not clearly cheaper or more effective than a simple feedback rule.

trigger_quality.justification: The description "Use for tasks." matches virtually every possible task, so it provides no real routing discrimination for when this skill should fire.
